method_notes: Weighted round of 32 performances most heavily as the freshest form signal, cross-referenced with group-stage goal difference and defensive records, then adjusted for extra-time fatigue (Paraguay, Morocco, Egypt all played 120+ minutes), host advantage for USA/MEX/CAN, and historical knockout pedigree.

predictions.reasoning: France have been the tournament's most complete side (GD+8, 3-0 in the R32) against a Paraguay team with two goals in four matches and 120 minutes in their legs.
Morocco's superior squad quality and proven knockout resilience edge Canada's home crowd, but the Netherlands shootout fatigue makes this tight and possibly another 120-minute grind.
Brazil's overall quality and group dominance outweigh Norway's counterattacking threat, though a defense that shipped seven in the group should concede once.
Mexico's perfect group and home crowd make this tight, but England's knockout experience and Mexico's long round-of-16 curse tilt it narrowly.
Spain haven't conceded all tournament and dismantled Austria 3-0, and their competitive record against Portugal in knockout settings favours them in a low-scoring Iberian derby.
Home advantage and a clean 2-0 knockout win tip a close match against a Belgium side that leaked two to Senegal, reversing the 2014 result.
Argentina's attacking edge (GD+7) faces an Egypt side running on fumes after a penalty shootout with just five goals scored all tournament.
A coin-flip between two disciplined defensive sides, but Colombia's meaner defense (one conceded in four matches) edges a Switzerland that has faced weaker attacking opposition.
